Watching from above, it wasn’t at all obvious before Calum Ritchie left the bench in Toronto last month that anything serious had happened. He knew right away, though, “that it was pretty bad,” after taking a hit from Nick Blankenburg that resulted in a lower-body injury.

That was five weeks ago, with a pit stop in Hamilton before Ritchie finally got back in an Islanders uniform on Wednesday evening against the Blues. The one-game AHL stint was mostly a function of wanting Ritchie to get back up to speed post-injury, though the organizational need created by Kyle Palmieri’s injury trumped that.

And, if absence has a way of clarifying one’s standing, this one seemed to drive home that, while Ritchie is still considered a foundational piece for the Islanders’ future, his presence in the lineup right now wasn’t so important that they couldn’t afford to have him do a de facto rehab stint in the AHL.

The Islanders didn’t plan on Ritchie being in the minors for any serious amount of time, but it was interesting, too, to hear coach Pete DeBoer say Wednesday morning that “in a perfect world, he might’ve had a little more runway there to get a few more games.”
news.content: پوشش های بیشتری را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. با مشاهده از بالا، قبل از اینکه کالوم ریچی ماه گذشته نیمکت نشین تورنتو را ترک کند، اصلاً مشخص نبود که اتفاق جدی رخ داده است. با این حال، او بلافاصله پس از زدن ضربه ای از نیک بلانکنبرگ که منجر به آسیب دیدگی پایین تنه شد، متوجه شد که «خیلی بد بود». این پنج هفته پیش بود، با یک پیت استاپ در همیلتون قبل از اینکه ریچی در نهایت با لباس جزیره ای ها در شامگاه چهارشنبه مقابل آبی ها بازگشت. حضور در یک بازی AHL عمدتاً تابعی از این بود که می‌خواستیم ریچی پس از مصدومیت به سرعت خود بازگردد، اگرچه نیاز سازمانی ایجاد شده توسط مصدومیت کایل پالمیری بر آن غلبه کرد. و، اگر غیبت راهی برای روشن کردن وضعیت فرد داشته باشد، به نظر می‌رسد که این یکی به خانه می‌آید که، در حالی که ریچی هنوز به عنوان یک قطعه اساسی برای آینده جزیره‌نشینان در نظر گرفته می‌شود، حضور او در ترکیب در حال حاضر آنقدر مهم نبود که آنها نتوانند از عهده او برآیند که یک دوره بازپروری عملاً در AHL انجام دهد. جزیره‌ای‌ها برنامه‌ای نداشتند که ریچی برای مدتی جدی در رده سنی‌ها حضور داشته باشد، اما جالب بود که می‌شنیدیم مربی پیت دیبور صبح چهارشنبه می‌گوید: «در یک دنیای عالی، او ممکن است کمی بیشتر در آنجا داشته باشد تا چند بازی دیگر داشته باشد.»

To celebrate our 225th birthday, The New York Post is highlighting the city’s icons: The people, places and things that make Gotham great.

Not all heroes wear capes — some draw them.

That would be Stan Lee, the creative force behind Spider-Man, Black Panther, Thor and countless other iconic comic book characters.

Lee’s own Marvel origin story started at 98th Street and West End Avenue. Born Stanley Martin Lieber in 1922, Lee was the son of Romanian Jewish immigrants. A curious kid with a mind faster than Iron Man’s jet pack, Lee tried every New York hustle as a teen — delivering sandwiches, ushering Broadway shows and manning a Garment District shop.

But Lee craved life as a Big Apple writer and landed his big break at Timely Comics at age 15. At first, he erased the pencil scratches from drawings. By 19, he was running the joint, and already put his stamp on Captain America’s famous shield-boomerang move.

During World War II, Lee served in the Army’s training film division, writing scripts for soldiers and working alongside entertainment legends Frank Capra and Theodor Geisel, a.k.a Dr. Seuss.

Then he traded American heroes for superheroes, returning to Marvel for good. It was Spider-Man, whom he co-created in 1962, which arguably had the biggest impact. The orphaned Queens teen bitten by a radioactive spider whose adventures challenged conventional ideas about youth, courage and family became an unofficial symbol of brave, loyal New Yorkers.

Lee died in 2018, but Spider-Man remains eternal. Next year, the web-slinger celebrates his 65th anniversary, still looking out for the city he calls home.
news.content: در نتایج جستجوی خود از پوشش ما بیشتر دیدن کنید. نیویورک پست برای جشن تولد 225 سالگی، نمادهای شهر را برجسته می کند: مردم، مکان ها و چیزهایی که گاتهام را عالی می کنند. همه قهرمانان شنل نمی پوشند - برخی آنها را می کشند. این می تواند استن لی، نیروی خلاق پشت مرد عنکبوتی، پلنگ سیاه، ثور و تعداد بی شماری دیگر از شخصیت های داستانی مارپیچ باشد. خیابان 98 و خیابان وست اند. لی با نام استنلی مارتین لیبر در سال 1922 متولد شد و پسر مهاجران یهودی رومانیایی بود. لی یک بچه کنجکاو با ذهنی سریع‌تر از جت پک مرد آهنی، در نوجوانی همه کارهای نیویورک را امتحان کرد - تحویل ساندویچ، راه‌اندازی نمایش‌های برادوی و راه اندازی فروشگاهی در منطقه پوشاک. اما لی هوس کرد زندگی به عنوان یک نویسنده اپل بزرگ داشته باشد و در 15 سالگی به موفقیت بزرگ خود در تایملی کمیک رسید. در 19 سالگی، او مشترکا را اداره می کرد و قبلاً مهر خود را بر حرکت معروف سپر-بومرنگ کاپیتان آمریکا گذاشته بود. در طول جنگ جهانی دوم، لی در بخش فیلم آموزشی ارتش خدمت می کرد، برای سربازان فیلمنامه می نوشت و در کنار اسطوره های سرگرمی، فرانک کاپرا و تئودور گیزل، معروف به دکتر مارهای آمریکایی، قهرمانان فوق العاده خوب را به جای قهرمانان عوض می کرد. مرد عنکبوتی بود که او در سال 1962 با هم خلق کرد، که مسلماً بیشترین تأثیر را داشت. نوجوان یتیم کوئینز که توسط یک عنکبوت رادیواکتیو گاز گرفته شد، ماجراجویی‌هایش ایده‌های مرسوم در مورد جوانی، شجاعت و خانواده را به چالش کشید و به نماد غیررسمی br تبدیل شد.

news.content: پوشش های بیشتری را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. «فصلی است که در پخش جریانی صرفه جویی زیادی می کنید. تقریباً جمعه سیاه است و معاملات در نوسان کامل هستند. آنها در محصولات فیزیکی نیز متوقف نمی شوند. معاملات پخش جریانی جمعه سیاه برخی از بهترین‌های امسال هستند. از یک سال HBO Max با 50٪ تخفیف و تا 75٪ تخفیف بر افزونه های Prime Video گرفته تا یک سال کامل Disney+ و Hulu با فقط 60 دلار، هیچ محدودیتی برای همه نمایش ها و فیلم های شگفت انگیزی که با امتحان کردن برخی از خدمات جدید پیدا خواهید کرد، وجود ندارد. در زیر، ما انواع خدمات مختلف را گردآوری کرده ایم که پیشنهادات عالی ارائه می دهند (امسال فقط برای تعطیلات جمعه سیاه در دسترس است. نوامبر 30)، بنابراین اجازه ندهید آنها از کنار شما عبور کنند. فقط با 5 دلار در ماه، یک سال کامل از Disney+ و Hulu دریافت کنید — دو سرویس عالی، یکی قیمت پایین. درست به موقع برای فصل جدید «The Pitt» (برای اولین بار در 7 ژانویه)، HBO Max برای یک سال تمام تخفیف نصف ارائه می دهد.Paramount+ — home of the Sheridan-and the King، که شامل «L-Sheridan-Averse» و «L-Seridan-anding,» و «L-Seridan-Averse» و «شریدان» است. "Frisco King" - فقط 2.99 دلار برای دو ماه اول شما است. سطح ممتاز بدون آگهی نیز در این معامله گنجانده شده است. در شش ماه Apple TV صرفه جویی زیادی کنید، که به شما زمان کافی می دهد تا با برنامه هایی که همه درباره آنها صحبت می کنند هماهنگ شوید - "Widow's Bay"، "Nocturne" - و خیلی چیزهای دیگر. همه برنامه های DIRECTV در حال حاضر در معرض فروش هستند! همه چیز را تماشا کنید، از جمله ورزش‌های محلی زنده، با طرح انتخابی مورد علاقه ما، که در حال حاضر 45 دلار تخفیف در دو ماه اول شما پس از پنج روز دارد.

news.originalContent:
Government says there is ‘no truth’ to media reports that Iraqi army units were moving towards the Kurdistan region.

Iraq’s government has denied local media reports that army units were moving towards the Kurdistan region, as a top court backed Baghdad’s authority over the region’s border crossings and oil in a deepening dispute with Erbil.

Government spokesperson Haidar al-Aboudi told state broadcaster Al-Iraqiya on Wednesday that there was “no truth” to the media reports. He said oil smugglers were diverting “tens of billions” into “private pockets and accounts”, and that the salaries of Kurdistan’s public employees were not part of the dispute.

Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi said “national sovereignty is indivisible” and that protecting Iraq’s wealth was “a battle for existence” in which the state would end all forms of smuggling.

Al-Zaidi has ordered the Border Ports Authority to take over all crossings in the Kurdistan region and to close unofficial crossings. He has also ordered federal authorities to take over oil fields in Kirkuk, Nineveh, Salahuddin and Diyala that are under Kurdish security control.

Iraq’s Federal Supreme Court has issued an interpretive ruling affirming federal powers to secure international borders and deploy armed forces across all Iraqi territory. It also affirmed Baghdad’s right to oversee border crossings, including those in Kurdistan, the production and export of oil and gas, and both oil and non-oil revenues.

Border Forces Commander Mohammed Abdul Wahab Sukkar al-Saidi told the state-run Iraqi News Agency on Thursday that the command had “begun implementing the directive of the commander-in-chief of the armed forces to close all unofficial crossings” with neighbouring countries.

He did not say how many crossings would be affected.

The Kurdistan Regional Government’s council of ministers, chaired by Prime Minister Masrour Barzani, said it rejected “any attempt to return Iraq to a centralised system”. Kurdistan Region President Nechirvan Barzani rejected addressing the region in “military language”, saying this “does not solve any problem”.

Thousands of people gathered in Erbil, the capital of the Kurdish region, on Thursday to protest against the government’s plan to take over border crossings and oil operations.

Reporting from Erbil, Al Jazeera’s Mahmoud Abdel Wahed said the protesters claim the government’s plan “touches on their sovereignty and their territorial integrity, and that this undermines the constitutional rights of the Kurdish people”.

“The question now is whether or not the government of Baghdad will be able to solve this peacefully without triggering a new chapter of conflict, a new political and economic confrontation with the Kurdish region.”

Baghdad says some 200,000 to 230,000 barrels of oil a day are being smuggled, worth about $200m a month, Al Jazeera correspondent Suhaib al-Asa said.

Salim Zakhour, a researcher in constitutional law and political systems, told Al Jazeera that the ruling, issued within 24 hours at al-Zaidi’s request, gave Baghdad a legal basis to act. “The court’s decision is final and decisive,” he said. “But the issue is not only constitutional and legal. There is a political problem.”

The country’s four presidencies have agreed to hold a national dialogue on December 1 to resolve the crisis.

The orders followed an investigation into smuggling at the state-run North Oil Company, after which al-Zaidi dismissed eight officials, including Kirkuk’s police chief and operations commander.

news.originalContent:
Egypt has suffered another tragedy as a deadly road explosion kills 31 and injures dozens.

An explosion rocked a highway in Cairo when a fuel truck overturned and caught fire, killing at least 31 people on Wednesday.

Egypt’s public prosecutor has announced an investigation into the crash, and the Ministry of Health said it will continue to monitor the situation.

But Egypt is no stranger to deadly accidents on its roads, despite spending billions of dollars on its transportation systems.

So what exactly caused the explosion and how unsafe are Egypt’s roads?

On Wednesday evening, a fuel tanker travelling on a busy ring road in Giza’s Imbabah district, a highly populated, working-class part of the Greater Cairo area, crashed and exploded, causing a fire that killed at least 31 people and injured 21 others.

Local media have reported that the explosion happened after the truck driver swerved to avoid a high-voltage cable which fell in front of the vehicle.

Twenty-seven vehicles were caught up and burned in the accident, according to Egypt’s judicial office.

Thirty-nine ambulances were dispatched to the scene, taking the injured to nearby hospitals for treatment, the Health Ministry said.

Egypt’s public prosecutor announced that there will be an investigation into the crash and ordered DNA samples from victims.

Egypt, which has a population of around 120m, is known for its dangerous roads. It clocked up a total of 44,940 road deaths and 476,126 injuries between 2019 and 2025, according to the Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS).

Last year, more than 5,800 road deaths and 84,000 road injuries were recorded by the agency, with pedestrians making up more than one-third of those killed.

Children under the age of 15 made up 1,580 of the deaths and 29,101 of the injured.

A World Bank report in 2020 found that the incidents occur because 97 percent of Cairo’s streets lack traffic lights and 78 percent of them have no clear pedestrian footpaths.

In 2025, there were 170 train incidents recorded, resulting in the deaths of 44 people and injuries to 215.

Earlier this month, at least seven people were killed and more than 125 others injured when a train backed into another, also in Giza, triggering calls for political accountability.

Egypt’s Ministry of Transport said that approximately $37bn was spent on transport investment between 2014 and 2024, but recurring incidents have raised questions about the effectiveness of this project.

The leader of the centrist Reform and Development Party’s parliamentary bloc, Irene Saeed, called for full financial transparency on how the Ministry of Transport spent its funding and loans in 2016.

A member of the Egyptian Parliament and leader of the Justice Party, Abdel Moneim Imam, told Al Jazeera earlier this month that the continued “turning of a blind eye to the shortcomings and the recurrence of accidents without genuine accountability leads to the continuation of the crisis”.

news.originalContent:
The Jewish Network for Palestine says the complete ban on Hamas was being used to stifle free speech and to target its members.

The Jewish Network for Palestine (JNP) has filed an application to reverse the proscription of Hamas under Britain’s Terrorism Act, arguing that the ban is being used against its members and is hampering freedom of speech in the United Kingdom.

The JNP filed a formal de-proscription application on Thursday under Section 4 of the Terrorism Act, which oversees applications to remove a group from the UK’s list of banned organisations.

This follows the arrest of the 80-year-old son of Auschwitz survivors and the prosecution of a 72-year-old Jewish writer – both members of the JNP’s Steering Group – for pro-Palestinian and anti-Zionist speech.

The JNP was founded in 2018 by British members of the United States organisation Jewish Voice for Peace, a group which aims to bring together Jews and non-Jews who support Palestine. It is one of 11 Jewish and Jewish-led organisations that form the UK’s Jewish bloc for Palestine, which is frequently present at protests against Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza and pogroms in the West Bank.

According to the chair of the JNP, David Cannon, proscription of Hamas has made it near-impossible to openly discuss the events of October 7, 2023, when Hamas led an attack on villages and army outposts in southern Israel. In particular, the JNP says, it has been unable to talk publicly about false narratives that followed for fear of contravening the act.

“Now, all of these things needed to be discussed, but the UK government’s proscription of the political wing of Hamas has made referring to such evidence [of false reporting] risk the accusation of supporting Hamas, which is not what we’re saying. We’re saying that we want to discuss these issues,” he said.

In the days following October 7, when more than 1,000 people were killed, many stories about babies being killed by Hamas fighters and mass rapes were circulated in international media. There has been no evidence of these.

Cannon added that one of the group’s active members had resigned, fearing that what she could say would affect her immigration status if found to violate the act.

According to the application, the JNP has about 600 members and supporters.

The JNP’s application was filed five years to the day after the British government proscribed the whole of Hamas as a terrorist organisation.

Hamas’s armed wing had been banned in 2001, but in 2021 the then-Home Secretary Priti Patel extended the ban to cover the whole political group, describing the organisation as “fundamentally and rabidly anti-Semitic” and arguing that the proscription was required to protect the Jewish community.

The government did not, however, explain how the proscription of Hamas would protect the Jewish community in the UK. Instead, the JNP argues that the designation has now been used against the Jewish community it was supposed to protect.

The group also argues that the continued proscription of Hamas in its entirety was a “disproportionate interference with the rights of JNP and its members” under the European Convention on Human Rights Articles 9, 10 and 11 on freedom of thought, expression and assembly, with the burden of the proscription falling on people in Britain.

Finally, they argue, Hamas has “no presence in the UK and has not been shown to pose a specific threat to it”.

“The less intrusive position that applied before November 2021 shows that proscription of the whole organisation is not necessary. On a proper application of the policy, and with the impact on JNP weighed, continued proscription is not justified,” the application stated.

Following the JNP’s application, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmoud has 90 days to consider it beginning the day after it is received. If it is refused, the group can appeal the decision.

Tony Greenstein, 72, an anti-Zionist writer and blogger and prominent member of the JNP, was prosecuted for publishing a blog on October 7, 2023, titled “Full Support for the Gaza Ghetto Uprising”, in which he evoked the Jewish Warsaw Ghetto Uprising in 1943.

While his post only mentioned Hamas in passing, in November 2024 Greenstein was charged under section 12 of the British Terrorism Act with inviting support for Hamas on the basis of one sentence in that blog and for writing “please share” on social media, promoting the piece.

After nearly three years and appearances in different courts, Greenstein was acquitted in August this year.

“If you can’t actually say what you think about an organisation without watching over your shoulder in case you’re contravening some law, then that’s chilling free speech, and that is the real issue,” Greenstein told Al Jazeera.

“That’s been made time and time again about the Terrorism Act. It’s really about clamping down on free speech,” he added.

During the criminal proceedings against him, five banks and building societies closed his accounts.

In Greenstein’s view, arresting Jews is not the best way to protect the Jewish community in the UK.

“It’s a very good way of protecting Zionism and the Zionists, and that is the difference,” he said. “The way they dress up their foreign policy choices is by saying they’re protecting a particular community. The reality is, of course, banning or proscribing Hamas has nothing at all to do with racist attacks against Jews, they’re completely separate phenomena.”

He added: “Hamas doesn’t operate in Britain. It never has operated in Britain …So how can we be at risk of being attacked by a group that doesn’t even exist here? It was about stopping people expressing an opinion on what’s happening in Gaza and in the occupied territories. That’s a very different thing.”

One of the founders of the JNP is Haim Bresheeth-Zabner, an 80-year-old Jewish-Israeli anti-Zionist filmmaker and film studies professor at the School of African and Oriental Studies (SOAS).

He was arrested and held for 13 hours in November 2024 immediately after he made a speech at a protest in Swiss Cottage, north London. It was part of wider protests held weekly by the International Jewish Anti-Zionist Network with the JNP’s involvement against the Israeli ambassador and the actions of the Israeli government in Gaza. In his speech, Bresheeth-Zabner said that the Israeli army “cannot fight the resistance” and “cannot win against Hamas … against Hezbollah …[or] against the Houthis”.

“They [the police] refused to discuss with me what I said that is considered applicable under the Terrorism Act. It took many hours of waiting in a very cold car park … I’m 80 … I have heart failure and cancer. So I wasn’t feeling all that well, but that didn’t make a difference. I also told them that I need to take my medications in the early evening, and they disregarded that,” Bresheeth-Zabner told Al Jazeera.

While he was not charged following his arrest, he said the ban has been used against people who want to speak up against the genocide in Gaza, making it impossible to criticise the Israeli army.

“This is a really odd situation where Britain, as a society, as a politicised society, as a country, as a regime, if you want, is not acting to uphold international law, and is proscribing our ability to speak against the genocide, to speak against Zionism, to speak against Israel. When we do that, we are arrested. We are charged,” he said.

“We’re [the JNP] supporting human rights, and human rights include the right to oppose a genocide, not just our right to oppose a genocide, but of course the rights of the victims of the genocide to resist it.”

news.originalContent:
New policy threatens further tariff hikes on China, India, Vietnam if trade negotiations fall through.

United States President Donald Trump’s administration has proposed a new slate of trade tariffs against 14 of the US’s key trading partners, including China, India and the European Union.

The tariffs, which would go into effect next year, will hit China the hardest, potentially subjecting its products to a 40 percent import tax.

Washington says the tariffs, announced by the US Trade Representative (USTR) on Wednesday, are a response to unfair trading practices which harm US manufacturing, including “excess industrial capacity” – subsidies and policies that enable manufacturers to overproduce and undercut the US.

But Trump has long used tariffs as leverage in trade negotiations.

So, is the latest tariff announcement an effort to win concessions in upcoming trade deals? Here’s what we know:

The tariffs would be imposed on products from China, Bangladesh, Cambodia, the EU, India, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam, according to the USTR. The maximum rates facing each country range from 20 percent to 40 percent.

It is unclear when exactly the tariffs would take effect, but a senior US official told the AFP news agency they would likely start in January at the earliest.

Trump has launched several rounds of trade tariffs against other countries and economies during his second term in office, with his administration citing various laws and justifications for the policies each time.

In April 2025, Trump imposed a sweeping raft of import taxes against almost all US trade partners, known as the “Liberation Day” tariffs. He said the measures were retaliation for unfair trade practices, including high tariffs, against the US that hurt local manufacturing. Trump imposed those tariffs under an emergency powers law, but the Supreme Court struck them down in February this year.

Then, in July, Washington cited a different law – section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 – to impose more tariffs on more than 80 countries. This time, Trump’s administration claimed the targeted countries had failed to adequately restrict imported goods made with forced labour.

The latest tariff announcement also cites section 301 of the same trade act, which allows Washington to penalise countries it determines are treating US businesses unfairly. It follows an eight-month investigation into what Washington calls “structural excess capacity”, by which governments give their industries unfair advantages with subsidies, suppressed wages and other policies.

Jamieson Greer, the US trade representative, told CNBC that many US trading partners were using “market distorting practices that tilt the trade balance in their favour while eroding America’s manufacturing base”.

Inga Fechner, a senior economist at ING THINK, wrote that “while the legal justification for tariffs keeps changing, US protectionism is becoming increasingly difficult to unwind.”

For several targeted countries, that appears to be a big factor.

The tariff announcement comes as the US negotiates trade agreements with several of the targeted countries, including China, India, Vietnam and Singapore, with some of the proposed tariff rates explicitly linked to the outcome of those talks.

China’s tariffs are due to rise by 20 percent, respecting a cap under a current US-China trade truce. But if talks to secure a new trade deal fail by January 10, when that truce is due to expire, the rate could double to up to 40 percent, according to USTR.

Vietnam would also be subject to a capped tariff rate of 20 percent if it makes a trade deal with Washington, which it is actively negotiating. But if those negotiations fall through, its rate would jump to 35 percent.

India would face a 17 percent tariff rate if a trade agreement is reached with Washington, but a 25 percent rate if not.

Singapore faces a 10 percent tariff if it reaches a trade deal with the US, but a 20 percent rate if not.

Madeline Chalecki, assistant director at the Atlantic Council’s GeoEconomics Center, said the US is also exercising leverage over Mexico, which Trump recently said the US is close to concluding a trade deal with. Mexico was among the countries included in the USTR’s excess capacity investigation, but has not yet been hit with new tariffs.

“The threat of additional tariffs may be a better negotiating chip than the duties themselves,” the Atlantic Council quoted Chalecki as saying.

Mona Paulsen, an assistant professor at the London School of Economics and Political Science Law School, told Al Jazeera that beyond tariffs, the bigger worry regarding US trade negotiations is whether they are “from the beginning, an asymmetrical exercise more calibrated to US economic growth, and less one about two (or more) partners cooperating”.

Some of the targeted countries or blocs have criticised the US’s new tariffs, while others have pledged to step up efforts to pursue trade deals with the US.

China’s Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun accused the US of engaging in “political manipulation”, saying the “so-called ‘overcapacity’ is a false issue”. Commerce Ministry spokesman He Yadong called on the US to “correct its erroneous practices” and said Beijing reserves the right to “take necessary measures” in response.

Singapore also called on the US to reevaluate ⁠the policy, which it expressed disappointment over.

India said any trade concerns between it and the US should be resolved in ongoing trade negotiations.

Vietnam said it was working to conclude a trade pact with the US and promised to address the “overcapacity” issue and to improve forced labour regulations.

The EU’s trade commissioner, ⁠Maros Sefcovic, ⁠said he strongly opposed the US tariff move, adding that Washington must abide by the 15 percent tariff limit it has already agreed for goods imported from the bloc.

Several analysts say Trump is trying to set up a long-term tariff infrastructure, despite the Supreme Court striking down his “Liberation Day” tariffs earlier this year.

Josh Lipsky, vice president and chair of international economics at the Atlantic Council, said the Trump administration’s latest announcement appears to be an attempt to set up a “tariff web – one meant to stick past this administration”.

Gregory Shaffer, professor of international law at the Georgetown University Law Center, told Al Jazeera that Trump is trying to “set tariffs globally” without having to deal with Congress.

US Senator Ron Wyden, a Democrat who is expected to chair the Senate Finance Committee in next year’s Congress, called the tariff move “a blatant attempt by Donald Trump to reconstruct his illegal global tariffs”.

“Global overcapacity is a serious problem, but Trump’s unilateral price-hiking tariffs are not the solution,” said Wyden.
news.content:
سیاست جدید افزایش بیشتر تعرفه‌ها بر چین، هند و ویتنام را در صورت شکست مذاکرات تجاری تهدید می‌کند. دولت دونالد ترامپ، رئیس‌جمهور ایالات متحده، فهرست جدیدی از تعرفه‌های تجاری را علیه 14 شریک تجاری کلیدی ایالات متحده از جمله چین، هند و اتحادیه اروپا پیشنهاد کرده است. این تعرفه‌ها که از سال آینده اجرایی می‌شود، بیشترین ضربه را به چین وارد می‌کند و احتمالاً 40 درصد محصولات این کشور را مشمول مالیات بر واردات می‌کند. واشنگتن می‌گوید تعرفه‌هایی که روز چهارشنبه توسط نماینده تجاری ایالات متحده (USTR) اعلام شد، پاسخی به شیوه‌های تجاری ناعادلانه است که به تولیدات ایالات متحده آسیب می‌رساند، از جمله «ظرفیت صنعتی مازاد» - یارانه‌ها و سیاست‌هایی که تولیدکنندگان را قادر می‌سازد تا بیش از حد تولید کنند و کمتر از آمریکا تولید کنند. اما ترامپ مدت‌هاست که از تعرفه‌ها به عنوان اهرمی در مذاکرات تجاری استفاده می‌کند. این چیزی است که ما می دانیم:
طبق گزارش USTR، این تعرفه ها بر محصولات چین، بنگلادش، کامبوج، اتحادیه اروپا، هند، اندونزی، ژاپن، کره جنوبی، مالزی، سنگاپور، سوئیس، تایوان، تایلند و ویتنام اعمال خواهد شد. حداکثر نرخ های پیش روی هر کشور از 20 درصد تا 40 درصد متغیر است. مشخص نیست که این تعرفه ها دقیقاً چه زمانی اعمال می شوند، اما یک مقام ارشد آمریکایی به خبرگزاری فرانسه گفت که این تعرفه ها احتمالاً زودتر از ماه ژانویه آغاز خواهند شد. ترامپ در دوره دوم ریاست جمهوری خود، با دولتش، چندین دور تعرفه های تجاری را علیه سایر کشورها و اقتصادها اعمال کرده است.

Rachel Accurso, the progressive children’s content creator known as Ms. Rachel, is now turning to explicit language over the conflict in Gaza.

“We made enough money for our lives, so I can say anything I want, and I do, like, acknowledge the people who spoke out a long time ago and lost their jobs and didn’t have that,” Accurso told podcast host Hasan Minhaj.

“Like, they were the brave ones. They were amazing. But, like, I’m sorry, that is so f–ked up. I never swear, but I’ve started swearing because I’m like …”

“I’ll see something, and I’ll just be like, how is this possible?” she continued. “Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch, the UN — they’re not wrong. B’Tselem, I met with them, the Israeli human rights org.

“They’re so clear that this is genocide, and you’re going to be mad that Macklemore says to end the genocide? That’s a great thing to say when there is a genocide.”

Accurso, who has been an outspoken critic of Israel’s actions in Gaza, appeared on Wednesday’s installment of the “Hasan Minhaj Doesn’t Know” podcast and was asked about her condemnation of music superstar Ed Sheeran, who she accused of caving to pressure after his opening act, Macklemore, was pushed out of Sheeran’s tour for chanting “Free Palestine” at a concert.

“I see people prioritizing language over children’s lives. And I’m not going to play about that,” Accurso said. “Because children’s lives, Palestinian children’s lives matter, and they’re still being killed every day. …

“When there’s a genocide going on, a genocide which we all have a duty to speak out against — actually, countries have a duty to stop a genocide.”

The YouTube star shrugged off “Free Palestine” being a controversial slogan and insisted celebrities not speaking out against the war in Gaza is “costing people’s lives.”

She insisted speaking out was “the best thing of my life” despite whatever backlash she has faced.

Accurso, who has millions of followers on social media with her songs and educational videos for children, has frequently posted about the conflict and condemned celebrities she feels don’t use their platforms to advocate for Gazans.

“Do you want to meet insert huge celeb? Me: No,” she wrote last month in an Instagram post. “I don’t fan girl over someone who is doing nothing during a genocide.”

Macy’s is making a major comeback just in time for the holidays, and you’re in luck, because they just released major deals.

For one of the best Black Friday sales, the popular retailer is releasing impressive deals on clothing, accessories, shoes, furniture and more for both men and women. Macy’s jewelry, in particular, is a Post Wanted favorite for winter, and we’re so excited to see some of our favorite pieces marked down.

Below, shop some of the best deals from Macy’s Black Friday Sale — whether you’re inclined to treat yourself or gift a loved one this holiday season.

Here at The Post, we don’t just diligently fact-check to call out fake news — we also relentlessly price-check to get you inflation-beating bargains you can trust. Before recommending a sale or purchase, our experienced bargain hunters put every “deal” through our price-checking gauntlet:

This Post readers’ favorite seems to be on everyone’s Christmas list this year. Shop in sterling silver, gold-plated sterling silver or rose gold-plated sterling silver before it sells out.

In a sea of stunning diamonds on Macy’s, it’s easy to forget about their extensive women’s watch selection. This rose gold, stainless steel design features a unique watch face with a collage of “G” logos.

Diamonds are a girl’s best friend, especially when they’re nearly 70% off. Shop this scintillating stunner in 14-karat white, yellow or rose gold.

Watch geeks will love this classic chronograph, complete with quartz movement and an embossed leather strap. Worried about wearing it in the snow? It’s water-resistant up to 330 feet.

This lab-grown tennis bracelet, set in sterling silver, shines so bright, you can spot it from across the room. I’d argue you can wear it on the daily; why reserve it for holiday parties only?

I’ve never been crazy about bold earrings, and these studs are a simple way to elevate an everyday look. Even better, the diamonds are tarnish-resistant, hypoallergenic, nickel-free, cadmium-free and lead-free.

More of a gold girl? Glisten in this thin, lightweight chain bracelet. It has a barely-there feel and stays secure thanks to a lobster clasp closure.

My boyfriend has been eyeing Seiko watches for the holidays, and I’ve got my eyes on this stainless steel design. It’s water-resistant and has a powerful battery life, ideal for snowy winter vacations.

You can’t have a tennis bracelet without a matching necklace. It’ll be hard to take your eyes off the sparkly lab-grown sapphires.

You can’t go wrong with a classic gold chain necklace. This style screams luxury, and it’s on sale for well under its typical $1,600-plus price.

I’m sorry, but ugly Christmas sweaters have never been my thing. This cozy, alpine green crewneck is holiday-festive and cute. Pair it with a maxi skirt for your holiday party, or rock it with jeans while ice skating this winter.

You can never have too many base tees. This pack of five sweat-wicking, cotton jersey crewnecks is available at a major discount right now. Shop, then style with just about everything in your closet.

Staying warm this winter shouldn’t be a hassle. Macy’s just dropped the price on a designer quilted puffer jacket, so you can enjoy Christmas activities sans shivering.

While you wait for cold weather and snow, enjoy these in-between temps in an acrylic-blend knit short-sleeve. It keeps you warm yet is breathable enough so that you won’t break a sweat.

Just because summer’s in the past doesn’t mean your T-shirts should hide at the back of your closet. Layer this one under a bomber jacket, coat or blazer in the fall.

A classic polo doesn’t have to come with a high price tag. This one streamlines an office look without you having to blow your budget. Available in 17 colors.

Rock with denim this season. Khloé Kardashian’s Good American jeans never disappoint, and this wide leg pair is especially chic and comfortable.

Don’t forget about pajamas amid cold weather. Cuddle up on the couch in this soft cotton flannel set, which comes in a playful pink striped print.

Men’s date-night attire can be tough to shop for, but we found a stylish, affordable option. Stand out in a designer quarter-neck, guaranteed to make your girl swoon.

Stay snug this winter in a plush 500-fill-power down jacket. It comes with a faux–fur–trimmed, detachable hood for a touch of après-ski style.

What’s winter without fleece? This lightweight, funnel-neck design comes in red, desert khaki, country ivory and more colors, both neutral and bold.

Designer on a budget? Count us in. This spacious purse converts to a crossbody and features a spacious interior to stash your phone, makeup and more during the day.

Looking for a neutral pair of boots with just the right amount of edge? These classic black booties stand out with the help of a gold “TH” logo. Plus, they feature a durable rubber outsole for optimal traction when walking outside in slippery snow.

If you’re expecting a lot of snow where you live, you’re going to need a sturdy shoe to prepare. These are waterproof with a warm, 200-gram insulation lining and chic faux fur trim.

We can’t resist the number of Michael Kors accessories on sale for the holidays. This design makes the perfect work tote, with a secure magnetic strap, luxe gold hardware accents and a hanging tag with the “MK” logo.

These men’s boots are sturdy, not bulky, with a cushioned, ethylene vinyl acetate footbed. They’re also moisture-wicking and easy to slip on if you find yourself running out the door often.

With holiday parties coming up, a chic pair of heels can come in clutch. We’re loving these classic, pointed-toe pumps, available in nude, black and red patent leather, as well as silver metallic.

Sandals aren’t solely reserved for summer. This pair features a sturdy block heel and ankle strap that’ll complement your Christmas dinner attire perfectly. Certain colors sell out fast, so make sure to shop ASAP.

Knee-high boots are an autumn staple, but I’ll be sporting mine all through the winter. This pair has a short-stacked heel that makes for comfortable, sturdy all-day wear.

Warm suede is trending for winter, and we recommend sporting it in the form of chic knee-high boots. They come in dark brown, black and dark natural, featuring a low flared heel.

New year, new fitness routine. Kick your exercise regimen into high gear with the help of these sports sneakers. They feature significant cushioning and support to reduce the impact on your muscles and joints while working out.

Give your bedroom the upgrade it deserves. This set includes a stylish comforter, sham, fitted sheet and more at an affordable discount. Available for twin, full, queen and king-sized beds.

The whole family deserves to lounge comfortably. Get some R&R with this upholstered sectional sofa. The seat and back cushions are removable and reversible

Good sleep is worth investing in — especially if a discount is involved. This mattress just dropped to its lowest price of the season. It includes three zones for lower back support and comfortable, breathable memory foam.

Sink into better sleep. This quilted, top-panel style has just the right amount of firmness to support the natural curvature of your body as you rest.

Behold the ultimate at-home work setup. It includes several file drawers, two outlets, removable dividers and a pull-out keyboard drawer.

Dressers can be super pricey, but I’ll admit, my bedroom wouldn’t be the same without mine. Having ten drawers for storage keeps clothes off the floor and my space looking tidy at all times.

This luxe coffee table is an eye-catching upgrade to a simple living room aesthetic. It features gorgeous gold legs and tempered glass you can store mugs, books and more on top of.

A classic couch is the cornerstone of one’s living room. Melt into this three-seater’s life-changing cushioning and softness during your next binge-watch.

This cozy mini sofa features reversible, removable back and seat cushions to optimize comfort. It comes in 13 colors, including my favorite, heavenly mocha gray.

Catch a whiff of this designer perfume. Its pretty pink bottle is complemented by irresistible red berry and citrus cocktail notes.

This floral fragrance family gives off major feminine energy. We’re lusting over the delicious apricot blossom and coconut aromas, blended in a playful pink bottle.

A fragrance set makes the perfect holiday gift for the one who can’t choose which fragrance they like best. This collection includes Eternity, Obsession, and CK One, featuring floral, citrus and musky scents.

If you’ve been wanting to splurge on designer perfume, now’s your chance while this one is on sale. Valentino’s luxe gold bottle is packed with notes of bergamot and gardenia.

Why have one designer perfume when you can try multiple? The man in your life will love and appreciate this set, which includes Devotion for Men, K Pour Homme Intense, Light Blue Pour Homme and The One for Men.

Want to smell good on the go? These portable perfume sprays are perfect to stash in a travel bag during upcoming holiday vacations.

One of my favorite parts about collecting fragrances is finding fun bottles that look cute on my dresser — like this one. It comes in a high-heel-shaped case and has notes of jasmine, cocoa and tonka bean.

Deck the halls with designer beauty. This gift set — featuring three Eau de Parfum and Eau de Toilette formulas — makes the perfect gift for a mom, sister or girlfriend this Christmas.

Are you a Billie Eilish fan? Channel your inner pop star with Billie’s signature fragrance, complete with bergamot, cardamom and fresh ginger.

Not only does this set include a fragrance, but it also features a hand cream, body lotion and mini perfume. Fruity notes of raspberry and Honeycrisp pear will have you reminiscing about summer.

As always, Black Friday falls the day after Thanksgiving. Get ready to shop ’till you drop on Friday, November 27.

Don’t want to wait? Early Black Friday deals start sooner than ever this November, and many are just as good (if not better than) the main event. Shop the most popular gifts and save from the comfort of your own home with our live updates on all Cyber Week savings.

The biggest online shopping moment of the year falls on Monday, November 30, 2026.

It depends! Black Friday shoppers may benefit from higher inventory on sell-out-risk items, while Cyber Monday may bring steeper discounts and incentives from some brands and retailers. We recommend making a strategic plan to maximize your savings without missing out on the items you want the most.

Jet-setters rejoice: Travel Tuesday, with its great deals on flights, hotels, cruises, all-inclusive resorts and more, will take place on Tuesday, December 1, 2026.

Absolutely! Black Friday and Cyber Monday bring some of the biggest sales of the year on big-ticket tech items such as AirPods, popular gifts like clothing and shoes, top kids toys and so much more.

Our New York Post shopping experts have decades of combined experience hunting for the biggest Black Friday and Cyber Monday savings on bestsellers across tech, beauty, clothing, home and more. All year round, we test the latest and greatest products, diligently price-check and recommend only the best deals for your coin. We research every “deal” to make sure mega sales aren’t just regular prices in disguise, and make sure you actually get the best discount on the web, while updating our coverage to reflect real-time trends and shopper needs. Our deals only feature legitimate retailers that we actually recommend, so you never have to worry about scams.

This article was written by Carrie Berk, Commerce Reporter for the New York Post. Carrie specializes in New York City-ready fashion finds for every style, age and budget. Combing the internet’s sale sections, brand collaborations, seasonal trends, timeless staples and lookalike styles, she makes recommendations that stand the test of time in your wardrobe – without breaking the bank. Before joining The Post full time in 2026, her work appeared in HuffPost, Women’s Health, Newsweek and more.

Looking for a headline-worthy haul? Keep shopping Post Wanted.

پوشش های بیشتری را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. Macy's درست در زمان تعطیلات بازمی گردد، و شما خوش شانس هستید، زیرا آنها به تازگی معاملات عمده ای را منتشر کرده اند. برای یکی از بهترین فروش های جمعه سیاه، خرده فروش محبوب، تخفیف های چشمگیری را در مورد لباس، لوازم جانبی، کفش، مبلمان و موارد دیگر برای مردان و زنان منتشر می کند. جواهرات میسی، به ویژه، یکی از جواهرات مورد علاقه Post Wanted برای زمستان است، و ما بسیار هیجان زده هستیم که برخی از قطعات مورد علاقه خود را علامت گذاری کرده اند. در زیر، برخی از بهترین معاملات را از فروش جمعه سیاه میسی خریداری کنید - خواه تمایل به پذیرایی از خودتان یا هدیه دادن به یکی از عزیزانتان در این فصل تعطیلات داشته باشید. در اینجا در The Post، ما فقط به شدت به این موضوع توجه نمی کنیم. قیمت را بررسی کنید تا بتوانید به قیمت‌هایی که می‌توانید به آن‌ها اعتماد کنید، قیمت‌گذاری کنید. قبل از توصیه خرید یا فروش، شکارچیان باتجربه ما هر "معامله" را از طریق دستکش بررسی قیمت ما انجام می دهند:
به نظر می رسد مورد علاقه خوانندگان این پست امسال در لیست کریسمس همه باشد. نقره عیار، نقره عیار با روکش طلا یا نقره استرلینگ رزگلد را قبل از فروش خریداری کنید. در دریایی از الماس های خیره کننده در Macy's، به راحتی می توان مجموعه گسترده ساعت های زنانه آنها را فراموش کرد. این طرح از رزگلد و استیل ضد زنگ دارای صفحه ساعت منحصربه‌فرد با کلاژی از آرم‌های «G» است. الماس‌ها بهترین دوست دختران هستند، به‌خصوص زمانی که نزدیک به 70 درصد تخفیف دارند. این شگفت‌انگیز درخشان را در رنگ‌های سفید، زرد یا رزگلد 14 عیار بخرید. علاقمندان به تماشای این کلاس را دوست خواهند داشت.

A Quince sale  — in this economy? Count us in.

Your favorite luxury-discount destination just got even cheaper. Yes, really. That’s right: As of Nov. 27, Black Friday 2026 has officially kicked off at Quince. And if you thought its already ridiculously good prices couldn’t get any better, think again.

Known for making the finer things in life a whole lot more affordable, Quince is slashing prices on all your favorites. We’re talking everything from festive, buttery-soft bamboo pajama sets and cozy down puffers to high-tech wellness gadgets, like red light therapy masks. Basically, your wishlist just got a lot longer.

Our team has tested out many of Quince’s best-sellers firsthand — including the dreamiest linen sheets and a handful of incredible Quince gifts — so we know what’s worth the buy. And let me tell you: there’s something for just about everyone at Quince.

Whether you’re treating yourself to a little self-care before the new year, finally upgrading your wardrobe, or hunting for a holiday gift that’ll impress even the pickiest person on your list, Quince’s Black Friday sale is the place to be.

I’ve rounded up the best Quince Black Friday deals across luggage, skincare, clothing, and more, so you can skip the endless scrolling and get straight to the good stuff.

Happy shopping (and saving)!

Winter is coming, and your wardrobe could use a cold-weather upgrade. Take an extra $35 off this Responsible Down Long Puffer Jacket, available in several versatile neutral shades. Designed to deliver insulating warmth, it’s the perfect layer for everything from running everyday errands to braving a snowy storm.

Bundle up! If you have big holiday travel plans coming up, now is the time to grab the durable, stylish and sleek Quince Carry-On & Medium Check-In Suitcase Set. Enjoy an extra $35 in savings with this smooth-rolling set that makes your airport treks that much easier.

Candles are a small thing that adds ambiance and personality to a space. This one has notes of citrus, clove, ginger, holly berry, pine and vanilla sugar. Enjoy an extra 25% off during Black Friday.

Santa came early! This adorable Tender Leaf Timber Taxi is on sale for Black Friday — and arguably, one of the cutest gifts you can put under the tree this year. It’s an adorable Montessori-inspired find for the creative kiddo in your life.

All these holiday plans have you exhausted? A caffeine boost is coming your way! This sleek coffee maker by Fellow whips up a smooth, rich brew time after time. And, the best part: it’s discounted during Quince’s Black Friday Sale.

A genuine leather bomber at this price? That’s a wardrobe win. Quince’s oversized silhouette delivers that coveted off-duty model look, while the premium leather construction makes it a timeless investment you’ll reach for season after season.

Get those pearly whites! The viral (and stunning) Marvis Whitening Mint Toothpaste is on sale at Quince for a limited time. Now’s the perfect time to grab this two-pack for a brighter, whiter smile ahead of the holidays.

Why buy three serums when one can tackle multiple complexion concerns? Murad’s Rapid Dark Spot Correcting Serum targets stubborn dark spots while helping improve the look of uneven tone, dullness and rough texture. Its brightening formula makes it a smart addition for anyone looking to streamline their skincare routine without skimping on targeted care.

Classic diamond studs, minus the eye-watering traditional markup. These 14K gold solitaire earrings feature lab-grown diamonds in a timeless four-prong setting, making them an elegant everyday staple or a seriously special gift.

Cold-weather dressing just got a whole lot more affordable. This cozy down-filled puffer combines insulating warmth with wind-resistant fabric to help keep chilly days comfortable. It’s a practical winter essential with the kind of markdown that makes upgrading your outerwear much easier to justify.

Consider this the moisturizer you’ll have to hide from everyone else in your household. Fresh’s Black Tea Ceramide Moisturizer delivers rich hydration while helping skin look firmer, smoother, and more nourished. It’s a luxurious daily cream that makes your skincare routine feel like an upgrade.

If you’ve been waiting to upgrade your bedding, this is your opportunity. Quince’s European linen sheets are loved for their breathable feel and relaxed, buttery-soft texture, making them an especially appealing choice for year-round comfort. Since these bestselling sheets rarely get discounted, this markdown makes the investment even sweeter.

Fuller-looking brows without the salon appointment? That’s the appeal of GrandeBROW. Its easy-to-use serum helps improve the appearance of sparse brows with consistent use, while the smoothing brush makes application effortless.

Get into the holiday cheer with this adorable, festive Christmas pajama set from Quince. The bamboo material is silky and soft on sensitive skin. Multiple patterns and colorways are available.

Your skincare routine just got a high-tech upgrade. The TheraFace Mask Glo offers hands-free LED treatments with red, red-plus-infrared, and blue light modes designed to address different skincare concerns, from visible signs of aging to blemish-prone skin.

Finally, a flossing upgrade you’ll actually want to use. The FLAUS Electric Flosser makes reaching tricky back teeth easier with a portable, waterproof design and gentle gliding floss heads. It comes with 45 replacement heads, a charging base, and a USB-C cable.

The next step to fresher, cleaner water for your faucets is on sale! The Filterbaby Skincare Filter 2.0 attaches directly to your faucet and helps reduce common impurities like chlorine and heavy metals that can contribute to skin irritation and dryness. Reviewers say it’s easy to install and use, and many report healthier-looking skin and hair after consistent use of this filter.

Make every move work a little harder with Bala Bangles. These adjustable wearable weights add comfortable resistance to Pilates, walking, dance workouts, and everyday movement. And they’re pretty cute, too!

Sunscreen just got a seriously fun upgrade. Vacation’s Classic Whip SPF 30 delivers broad-spectrum protection in an airy, whipped mousse that sprays out in playful star-shaped peaks. It’s retro-inspired, lightweight, and an easy way to make daily sun protection feel a little more like vacation.

Your next travel upgrade is officially more affordable. Quince’s carry-on combines smooth-rolling convenience, efficient packing space, and a clean minimalist design that looks far more expensive than its price tag. If a new suitcase has been on your travel wish list, this markdown makes now a particularly smart time to upgrade.

Big recovery benefits, travel-friendly size! The Theragun Mini delivers percussive massage therapy in a compact design, with three attachments, an ergonomic grip and simple one-button controls. Bluetooth connectivity pairs it with the Therabody app for personalized guidance, too.

Real silk, machine-washable convenience, and 25% off? This is one of the sale’s smartest wardrobe buys. The fluid drape makes it polished enough for a night out but versatile enough to layer under blazers, cardigans and everyday basics.

Designer-looking style for a fraction of the usual price. This bestselling crossbody pairs Italian leather with a classic quilted finish for a polished, elevated look that works from brunch to date night. At just $114, it’s one of the strongest luxury-for-less finds in the entire sale.

Hydration just got a Black Friday-worthy upgrade. Quince Recovery Electrolytes pack 1,000 milligrams of sodium, 250 milligrams of potassium, 100 milligrams of magnesium, and 2 milligrams of zinc into convenient, grab-and-go sticks. They’re sugar-free, stevia-free, and free of artificial ingredients.

Bring award-winning Italian design to your table with this stunning flatware set — now offered at its best market value, with an extra $70 in credit when you purchase.

Bring the spa experience home without the expensive appointment. The HigherDOSE Infrared Sauna Blanket features adjustable heat and a preset timer for a convenient at-home relaxation session. It’s designed to support relaxation and circulation, and reviewers love using it as their go-to wind-down ritual after a long day.

Fine jewelry rarely gets a meaningful markdown at Quince, making this $188 saving especially noteworthy. This 14K gold lab-grown diamond tennis bracelet delivers timeless sparkle and an effortlessly elegant look without the traditional fine-jewelry markup.

The perfect travel jacket just got even more tempting. This lightweight down layer packs down easily for suitcases and weekend bags while delivering cozy insulation when temperatures drop. Its streamlined, flattering fit means you get the warmth without the bulky puffer look.

A great chef’s knife can completely change your time in the kitchen, and this one is worth a closer look. Its fully forged German stainless steel construction delivers a balanced feel, dependable durability, and the precision needed for everyday chopping and slicing. At 20% off, it’s an especially worthwhile kitchen upgrade.

There’s never a dull moment in New York City. For the first time ever, Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed due to extreme weather conditions.

Heavy rain and strong winds are expected on Thanksgiving Day as a major nor’easter is set to wreak havoc on the East Coast. It’s important to note that the parade is postponed, not canceled.

“Due to the extreme weather conditions, the city of New York, Macy’s and NBC have decided, in the interest of safety for both the participants and spectators, to move the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday, Nov. 28,” an NBC spokesperson said in a statement.

The annual event has never been canceled due to weather, per the NY Post, but it was “squashed for three consecutive years during World War II.” Today’s telecast will feature a replay of the 2025 Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade.

It’s a tough day to be a giant Snoopy balloon, but we persist. When will the 2026 Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade air on NBC? Here’s everything you need to know.

The official telecast airs from 8:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. in all time zones on NBC and Peacock. But, as we mentioned above, due to “extreme weather conditions,” NBC has postponed the parade and will instead be reairing the 2025 Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade.

The parade will be followed by the 2026 National Dog Show at 12:00 p.m. ET.

Nope. It’s just postponed. The 2026 edition will air this weekend.

A Saturday Thanksgiving parade? Why not!? This year’s Macy’s parade will now air Saturday, November 28 at 8:30 a.m. on NBC and Peacock.

You can watch the 2026 Thanksgiving Day Parade live on NBC, NBC.com (with a cable login), or the NBC app.

The only way to watch shows airing live without cable is by using a live TV streaming service. Our favorite is DIRECTV, which comes with a five-day free trial before payment begins.

DIRECTV offers a number of flexible subscription options, including Genre Packs, so you can best choose which streaming plans fit your needs and budget. Packs start at $19.99/month.

You can also stream this joyous holiday event with an active subscription to fuboTV, Hulu + Live TV, YouTube TV, Peacock Premium, or Sling TV. FuboTV, YouTube TV, and Hulu + Live TV offer free trials for new subscribers.

Peacock currently offers two subscription types: Premium with ads and Premium Plus ad-free. Peacock Premium costs $12.99/month, while Premium Plus costs $19.99/month.

You can save a bit by subscribing to one of Peacock’s annual plans, which give you 12 months for the price of 10. These cost either $129.99 with ads or $199.99 without ads.

Peacock Premium Plus is also available to subscribe to via Prime Video with a seven-day free trial that you can’t get by subscribing directly on Peacock.

You can also bundle Peacock and Apple TV for $17.99/month or $22.99/month (ad-free on Peacock).

Peacock doesn’t directly offer a free trial, but thankfully, you can sample the streamer through Prime Video. Amazon offers a seven-day free trial of Peacock Premium Plus, which renews at $199.99/year until canceled.

You can also score a free subscription to Peacock through Instacart+, which offers a free trial. Finally, if you’re a DIRECTV subscriber, you can also get two months of Peacock Premium by adding the Movies Extra Pack.

Yes! Students can get Peacock Premium for $6.99/month for 12 months. Verification is required, and you can cancel anytime.

The 2026 Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade airs Saturday, November 28 from 8:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. in all time zones on NBC and Peacock.

news.originalContent:
Turkeys see a 26-percent price rise, forcing families to reconsider hosting and opt for potluck-style celebrations.

Across the United States, kitchens will fill with the smell of roasting turkey as Americans gather to celebrate the Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday.

Every family has its own traditions. Some swear by sweet potatoes topped with marshmallows. Others have carefully guarded family recipes for gravy, and there is always the perennial debate over pumpkin or pecan pie – and whether it should be served with a dollop of whipped cream or a scoop of ice cream.

But regardless of what makes it onto the Thanksgiving table this year, many Americans have something less appetising in common: a heftier grocery bill. The cost of a typical Thanksgiving meal is up 11 percent from last year, according to a new analysis by the think tank The Century Foundation.

The prices of many typical side dishes are up by double-digit percentages. Green beans are up 36.7 percent in price for a 1.5-pound bag, from $2.99 to $4.08 in a year’s time. Russet potatoes are up 6.8 percent for a five-pound bag, and Granny Smith apples, which are typically used in apple pie, are up 10.2 percent for a three-pound bag.

The centrepiece of the Thanksgiving table, the turkey, is also up by 26 percent compared with this time last year.

“Thanksgiving is supposed to be about gathering around the table, but this year many families are deciding how many people they can afford to feed,” Kyle Moore, chief economist at The Century Foundation, said in a statement.

Measuring just by the number of guests, the American Farm Bureau forecasts a rise of 6 percent for a 10-person meal, marking the first increase in price since 2022, when prices hit a record high, according to the report.

Some grocers are doing what they can to keep prices lower for consumers, including Baris Avci, who runs Green Valley, a small neighbourhood grocery store in the Bushwick neighbourhood of Brooklyn, New York.

“Some very important things like eggs, milk, sugar, we sell almost at cost. We don’t make much money, but we also have a certain percentage to [sustain] the business. Like how the people struggle, we struggle too,” Avci told Al Jazeera.

Higher prices mean that some shoppers are having to rethink their traditions. Sam Braverman, who was shopping at Green Valley, told Al Jazeera that in past years, his mother hosted Thanksgiving and took care of all the costs, but given price increases, his family is taking a different approach.

“Well, my ma is more open to kind of a potluck vibe this year, of people sort of bringing a few things,” Braverman told Al Jazeera.

“To make that same meal is going to be 130-150 percent of what it was last year, so you might as well accept some offerings.”

Heightened costs can stem from bottlenecks in the Strait of Hormuz because of the US-Israel war on Iran, which has led to a rise in the cost of both fuel and fertiliser needed in the food production supply chain.

During the spring planting season, prices for urea, which is used in fertilisers, jumped by as much as 50 percent when the war began, meaning that farmers needed to pay more for fertiliser. Those costs were ultimately passed down along the supply chain from farmers to warehouses and then onto supermarket shelves.

Tariff-driven pressures have also led to heightened costs. For example, tariffs on steel used in cans have caused prices to increase on canned goods for consumers. In September, Campbell’s Soup said it would raise prices by 4 to 5 percent on 60 percent of its products.

Some big-box retailers like Walmart, however, are using their economies of scale to cut prices for consumers. Every year, the Bentonville, Arkansas-based chain offers a holiday meal package that consumers can buy, which includes a complete holiday meal for 10 people. It will cost shoppers 12 percent less than the same deal last year.

For those bearing the brunt of the costs, that means more people are finding ways to borrow or at least scale back. A third of Americans who are planning on hosting this year say that doing so is putting them under financial strain, according to a report from LendingTree, an online loan marketplace.

As a result, nearly 62 percent of hosts say they’re going to borrow money to host this year – 18 percent of whom say they’re using what are called buy now, pay later (BNPL) loans, which are deferred payment plans for expenses.

Usage has jumped significantly in recent years, with 16 percent of Americans using BNPL loans, which are offered by fintech companies like Affirm and Klarna, marking a six-percentage-point jump since 2021, according to an August report from the US Federal Reserve.

It found that those with lower credit scores and lower incomes, as well as younger people and both Black and Hispanic adults, are more likely to use these services than the general population.

There are slightly fewer people travelling for Thanksgiving this year, too. The American Automobile Association (AAA) forecasts that more than 81.6 million Americans will travel, marking a slight decline of 121,000 travellers, including those travelling by plane, car, bus and train. The decline marks a reversal of the trend, as the number of travellers climbed over the last three years.

“After three years of record highs, the number of travelers is slightly lower, partly because of higher travel costs this year,” Stacey Barber, vice president of AAA Travel, said in a news release announcing the data.

Seven in 10 Americans are planning not to travel this holiday season at all, according to a report from the financial services company BNO, marking a 10-percent drop from this time last year.

While the average price for a gallon of petrol (3.78 litres) is down from last month – $3.61 on Tuesday versus $4.29 a month ago for regular fuel – it is still higher than this time last year, when it was $3.06, according to AAA’s daily fuel price tracker.

For those hitting the skies, domestic airfares rose 31 percent for Thanksgiving travel, averaging $402, according to a report released in September by the travel website Hopper, which tracks holiday travel trends, marking this Thanksgiving as the most expensive holiday travel season in a decade.

news.originalContent:
Despite navigating personal hardships, Ihab Abu Jazar calls it a ‘badge of honour’ to coach the Palestine football team.

For Ihab Abu Jazar, being the coach of Palestine’s national football team comes with burdens far heavier than sporting responsibilities.

His mind constantly returns to his family in Gaza, now displaced and living in tents amid Israel’s genocidal war on the Palestinian territory.

“Truthfully, it is difficult to carry out your professional responsibilities while your family and your people are living through such circumstances,” he told Al Jazeera earlier this month while in Doha.

“For me to coach the Palestinian national team, a team that represents this suffering, and to try to make it a source of joy, bring a smile to people’s faces or give the Palestinian people hope, means a great deal to me personally.”

The 46-year-old former footballer said it was a “badge of honour” to coach the national team, which he led to 2027 AFC Asian Cup qualification after taking the reins in 2024.

The team were drawn in Group A against Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and Oman, with the tournament rescheduled from January to December 2027 due to the ongoing conflict in the region.

Palestine have enjoyed considerable success in recent international friendlies, including a 2-2 draw with New Zealand, defeating Tajikistan 4-2, and thrashing China 5-0.

But the victories are bittersweet, given what’s happening at home.

He was in Algeria for a training camp with the national team when he received news that his house had been destroyed. His entire family now lives in al-Mawasi, a coastal area where more than 900,000 displaced people are sheltering in southern Gaza.

“The Palestinian people are suffering wherever they are,” Abu Jazar said.

He recounted an ordeal he went through before a qualifying match against Kuwait. Israel had issued a forced evacuation order for the area where his family lived, but his brother, Khalil, refused to leave.

“He had reached a point where he was simply saying, ‘Where am I supposed to go? Where can I possibly go?’” Abu Jazar recalled.

He made a last-ditch attempt to convince his brother to flee before boarding the team bus headed to the stadium for the match.

“I kept trying to call, but I could not get through. At that point, I had to trust that, God willing, my brother had listened to what I told him,” Abu Jazar said.

“We also had a match to play in the name of Palestine. We had to concentrate and do our job.”

Abu Jazar was able to breathe a sigh of relief after the match when he eventually got through to his brother, who assured him that they had all managed to leave safely.

A passion for sport is shared throughout Abu Jazar’s family. His mother, Huda, played volleyball at school and even offers her son tactical advice over the phone.

“Sometimes we talk about football and sports; she evaluates the players and discusses their performances after a match,” he said. “To be honest, she understands football very well in general.”

Abu Jazar’s message to the world is: “We are a people who simply want to live. We are a people with ambitions and hopes, a people with creative minds, thinkers, and scientists.

“And sport is also part of the culture and identity of any society. We, too, are sporting people; we are football-loving people.

“So, we ask the whole world to grant us our rights.”
news.content: ایهاب ابوجزار علیرغم تحمل سختی‌های شخصی، مربیگری تیم فوتبال فلسطین را «نشان افتخار» می‌نامد. برای ایهاب ابوجزار، مربیگری تیم ملی فوتبال فلسطین باری بسیار سنگین‌تر از مسئولیت‌های ورزشی دارد. ذهن او دائماً به خانواده‌اش در غزه بازمی‌گردد، که اکنون آواره‌ترین اسرائیلی‌ها در جنگ‌های فلسطینی هستند. قلمرو او اوایل این ماه در دوحه به الجزیره گفت: «راستش، انجام مسئولیت‌های حرفه‌ای‌تان در حالی که خانواده‌تان و مردمتان در چنین شرایطی زندگی می‌کنند، دشوار است.» «برای من مربی تیم ملی فلسطین، تیمی که این رنج را نشان می‌دهد، و سعی می‌کنم آن را به مایه شادی تبدیل کنم، لبخندی را به چهره مردم بیاورم یا به من امیدی بزرگ بدهم. این فوتبالیست سابق 46 ساله گفت که این یک "نشان افتخار" است که سرمربی تیم ملی باشد و او پس از در دست گرفتن کنترل در سال 2024 به مسابقات جام ملت های آسیا در سال 2027 منجر شد. این تیم در گروه A مقابل عربستان سعودی، کویت و عمان قرار گرفت و مسابقات از ژانویه به دسامبر 2027 تغییر کرد. فلسطین در بازی های دوستانه اخیر بین المللی موفقیت قابل توجهی داشته است، از جمله تساوی 2-2 با نیوزلند، شکست 4-2 تاجیکستان و شکست 5-0 چین. اما با توجه به اتفاقاتی که در خانه رخ می دهد، پیروزی ها تلخ هستند. او در الجزایر برای یک اردوی آماده سازی با تیم ملی در زمان حضورش در الجزایر بود.

news.originalContent:
Kenya’s High Court orders a halt to ⁠further works at the quarantine facility until the government discloses details of agreement with the US.

A court in Kenya has ruled that the government breached ⁠the constitution in allowing the ⁠construction of a United States-backed Ebola quarantine facility at a military airbase in the country.

High Court Judge Patricia Nyaundi said on Thursday that the government should have disclosed the details of the agreement with the US and sought public input before signing the deal on the facility near the town of Nanyuki in central Kenya.

The court ordered that any ⁠further works at the quarantine facility be stopped until the government meets these conditions.

“Put differently, the petitioners, the people of Kenya and more significantly, the residents of Laikipia County have been left with the position of persons standing outside the sealed wooden window, straining to discern what is ⁠taking place on the other side,” Nyaundi said in her ruling.

“They are aware ⁠that the decisions affecting their community are being made and implemented, yet they have been denied any meaningful opportunity to know, interrogate or participate in those decisions.”

The 50-bed ⁠facility, located inside Laikipia airbase near Nanyuki, was intended to quarantine people exposed to Ebola, including US citizens. Seven American aid workers who had been ‌in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) to help tackle the Ebola outbreak quarantined at the facility in July.

Kenyans have staged angry protests against the facility, as residents accuse the US of offloading Ebola risks onto Kenyans. In June, at least one person was killed after Kenyan police opened fire at demonstrators protesting against the facility.

The week before, hundreds took to the streets in Nanyuki amid growing frustration among residents as Kenyan and US authorities publicly reaffirmed their commitment to the plan despite court orders. At the time, the demonstration also turned violent, with at least two people killed and one wounded.

Kenya’s High Court had temporarily suspended the facility’s construction in late May, but it found ⁠that Health Minister Aden Duale failed to comply with the orders. Duale later told the court he had ordered an immediate halt to construction ⁠and related activity at the site.

Kenya reported its first imported case of the Bundibugyo Ebola ‌strain in early October in a traveller who had arrived from the DRC via Uganda. As of mid-November, Kenya had recorded two deaths and seven other cases, all of whom have recovered. No new cases ‌have been reported in Kenya since October 19.

There are no approved vaccines or treatments for the Bundibugyo strain responsible for the outbreak, which the World Health Organization declared an international public health emergency on May 17.

The government has not yet commented on Thursday’s court ruling.
news.content:
دادگاه عالی کنیا دستور توقف فعالیت‌های بیشتر در این مرکز قرنطینه را تا زمانی که دولت جزئیات توافق با ایالات متحده را فاش نکند، صادر کرد. دادگاه کنیا حکم می‌دهد که دولت قانون اساسی را نقض کرده است و اجازه ساخت پایگاه هوایی تحت حمایت ایالات متحده برای قرنطینه ابولا در یک کشور را داده است. پاتریشیا نیاوندی، قاضی دادگاه عالی، روز پنجشنبه گفت که دولت باید جزئیات توافقنامه با ایالات متحده را فاش می کرد و قبل از امضای قرارداد در مورد تاسیسات نزدیک شهر نانیوکی در مرکز کنیا باید نظر مردم را جلب می کرد. دادگاه دستور داد تا زمانی که دولت این شرایط را برآورده کند، هرگونه کار بیشتر در این مرکز قرنطینه متوقف شود. نیاوندی در حکم خود گفت: «به عبارت دیگر، درخواست‌کنندگان، مردم کنیا و مهم‌تر از آن، ساکنان شهرستان لایکیپیا در وضعیت افرادی قرار گرفته‌اند که بیرون پنجره چوبی مهر و موم شده ایستاده‌اند و تلاش می‌کنند تا آنچه را که در طرف دیگر در حال وقوع است تشخیص دهند. آنها می‌دانند که تصمیم‌هایی که بر جامعه آنها تأثیر می‌گذارد در حال اتخاذ و اجرا است، با این حال از هر گونه فرصت معناداری برای دانستن، بازجویی یا مشارکت در آن تصمیم‌ها محروم شده‌اند.»
این مرکز 50 تختخوابی، واقع در پایگاه هوایی لایکیپیا در نزدیکی نانیوکی، برای قرنطینه افراد در معرض ابولا، از جمله شهروندان آمریکایی، در نظر گرفته شده بود. هفت امدادگر آمریکایی که برای کمک به مقابله با شیوع ابولا در جمهوری دموکراتیک کنگو (DRC) بودند، در این مرکز در جو قرنطینه شدند.

news.originalContent:
Russian forces launch ballistic missile attack on Ukrainian capital Kyiv, hitting a shopping centre and other buildings.

At least five people have been killed and three others were wounded in a Ukrainian drone attack on Russian-occupied Zaporizhia, a Russian-installed official said, as Russian forces hit Ukraine’s capital Kyiv in a ballistic missile assault.

“Following an enemy drone attack on a parking lot, five people were killed and three others wounded in the locality of Vesioloye,” Moscow-installed governor Yevgeny Balitsky wrote on Telegram on Thursday.

Earlier, Ukrainian forces hit a major Russian military base east of Moscow, damaging five aircraft used to launch missiles and bombs, according to the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine.

Russian authorities also reported repelling drone attacks in the Tuymazinsky district in the Bashkortostan region and in the city of Nevinnomyssk in the Stavropol region.

Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, and fighting has continued despite a renewed US-backed push to end Europe’s worst conflict since World War II.

Russia has claimed the annexation of the southern region of Zaporizhia, which it partially controls, since September 2022.

The Ukrainian capital, Kyiv, was targeted with ballistic missiles late on Wednesday, striking a shopping centre and two other buildings on the east side of the Dnipro River bisecting the city, with warnings for residents to remain in shelters still in place, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said.

Russia’s Defence Ministry said on Thursday its forces had carried out a massive overnight strike on Ukraine, hitting military-industrial facilities in Kyiv, the Interfax news agency reported.

The Defence Ministry also said Russian forces had struck a dry cargo vessel southeast of Odesa in the Black Sea overnight, according to the news agency. The ministry alleged the ship was carrying military equipment and dual-use goods to Ukraine.

Al Jazeera’s Audrey MacAlpine, reporting from Kyiv, said the residents heard loud ballistic missile impact sounds late on Wednesday, which injured at least seven people.

“People who live in certain areas of the city that come under frequent attack, they go and spend their nights in the shelter, even before air raid sirens raise alarm,” she said. “Coming into this winter, Russia has really heightened its attacks, especially on energy facilities.”

Al Jazeera’s Yulia Shapovalova, reporting from Moscow, said Russia “is putting pressure on Kyiv’s military infrastructure, straining its air defences, and everything that can support military supply chains”.

“Russia has also been hitting power plants ahead of cold weather. The aim is to wear down morale and inflict economic damage, in addition to all these military effects,” she added.

Since Russia launched its full-scale invasion, MacAlpine said Ukraine’s energy capacity is below 40 percent of pre-war levels, as a number of the combined heating and power plants in Kyiv and the region have repeatedly gone offline due to attacks.

Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte urged Russia not to “expand the war” in Ukraine, in a joint statement issued on Wednesday after meeting in Florida.

“We also discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war, and the importance of obtaining a peaceful resolution to the war as rapidly as possible,” the statement added.

The joint appeal by Trump and Rutte comes after the US leader described Russian President Vladimir Putin as “my friend” during a meeting in China last week.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has taken issue with Trump’s comments on Putin.

“For us, he is a killer,” Zelenskyy told CNN.
news.content: حمله موشکی روسیه به کیف پایتخت اوکراین و اصابت یک مرکز خرید و ساختمان‌های دیگر. یک مقام مستقر در روسیه گفت که در حمله موشکی بالستیک به کیف پایتخت اوکراین، حداقل پنج نفر کشته و سه نفر دیگر زخمی شدند. یوگنی بالیتسکی فرماندار مستقر در مسکو روز پنجشنبه در تلگرام نوشت: «در پی حمله پهپاد دشمن به یک پارکینگ، پنج نفر در محله وسیولویه کشته و سه نفر دیگر زخمی شدند. به گفته ستاد کل ارتش اوکراین، پیش از این، نیروهای اوکراینی یک پایگاه نظامی روسیه را در شرق مسکو هدف قرار دادند و به پنج هواپیمای مورد استفاده برای پرتاب موشک و بمب آسیب رساندند. مقامات روسیه همچنین از دفع حملات هواپیماهای بدون سرنشین در منطقه تویمازینسکی در منطقه باشقورتوستان و شهر نویننومیسک در منطقه استاوروپل خبر دادند. روسیه در فوریه 2022 تهاجم تمام عیار خود را به اوکراین آغاز کرد و علیرغم تلاش مجدد ایالات متحده برای پایان دادن به بدترین درگیری اروپا از زمان جنگ جهانی دوم، جنگ ادامه یافته است. روسیه از سپتامبر 2022 مدعی الحاق منطقه جنوبی Zaporizhia است که تا حدی آن را کنترل می کند. کیف پایتخت اوکراین اواخر روز چهارشنبه با موشک های بالستیک هدف قرار گرفت و به یک مرکز خرید و دو ساختمان دیگر در سمت شرق رودخانه دنیپرو که شهر را به دو نیم کرده بود هدف قرار گرفت و هشدارهایی برای ساکنان این شهر برای ماندن در آن وجود داشت.
